patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been very fussy and has shown decreased interest in feeding for the past few days. His mother reports that despite the feeding difficulties, she believes the child has been gaining weight. There were no complications during birth at 39 weeks of gestation.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Crying, especially intense with abdominal palpation

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical or surgical history. Delivered vaginally at 39 weeks without complications.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: First child to young parents, no history of similar illness in the family.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: No episodes of fever, vomiting, or diarrhea. The baby has not had any known illnesses since birth.

objective_for_doctor: Diagnose the underlying condition based on clinical presentation and examination findings in an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Hi—my baby boy has been very fussy for a few days and doesn’t seem very interested in feeding. When I try to press on his belly, he cries a lot more, and his abdomen looks distended, though he still seems to be gaining weight.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any skin excoriations—like areas where the skin is scratched, rubbed raw, or has small open spots—anywhere on your body? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: No, I haven’t noticed any skin scratching, rubbed-raw areas, or open spots anywhere on his body.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any episodes where you stop breathing or you have pauses in breathing during sleep (for example, someone says you stop, or you wake up gasping)?
turns.patient_answer: “His breathing during sleep seems normal—no pauses or times where he stops breathing, and I haven’t noticed him waking up gasping.”

turns.doctor_question: After your minor injury, have you noticed any signs that a bone might be broken—such as severe pain, swelling, bruising, deformity, or trouble using the injured area? (Yes/No)
turns.patient_answer: “No—there hasn’t been any injury or any swelling, bruising, deformity, or trouble using an arm or leg; it’s mainly the belly that seems very painful when I touch or press it.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any redness or warmth on your **left wrist** (the skin looking red compared to the other side)?
turns.patient_answer: “No—there’s no redness or warmth on his left wrist, and I haven’t noticed any skin changes like that anywhere on him.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bruising on your chest wall (for example, dark or discolored areas on the chest), especially after an injury, coughing, or strain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bruising or dark/discolored areas on his chest wall, and we haven’t had any injury, heavy coughing, or straining that could’ve caused it.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been urinating much more than usual lately—like needing to go to the bathroom more often or producing a larger amount of urine?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed him urinating much more than usual—his wet diapers seem about the same in amount and frequency. It’s mainly the fussiness, reduced interest in feeding, and the belly looking distended, with him crying more when I press on it.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you used any substances such as alcohol, tobacco, cannabis, opioids, stimulants, or other drugs in the past or currently? (Yes/No)
turns.patient_answer: “No—there’s no tobacco, alcohol, cannabis, opioids, stimulants, or any other drugs in his or my use currently.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any trouble controlling your urine—such as leaking urine or not making it to the bathroom in time? (yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No—his wet diapers have been normal, and I haven’t noticed any leaking or loss of urine control. He hasn’t had any trouble reaching when he needs to pee.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any new or changing skin lesion or spot on your body (for example, a sore, bump, patch, mole change, or area that’s not healing)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any new or changing spots, bumps, sores, patches, or anything on his skin that’s not healing—his skin looks normal to me. It’s mainly his belly that seems painful when pressed, along with the fussiness and decreased interest in feeding.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any nosebleeds recently (even if they were mild or only happened once)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, there haven’t been any nosebleeds—mild or otherwise—and I haven’t noticed any bleeding from his nose at all.”
